newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Ifo sees growing unemployment in East.
newsitem.headline: German Ifo sees growing unemployment in East.

text.p: Six years after reunification, east German economic recovery is losing momentum and as many as 20,000 jobs in industry may be shed this year, a survey by the Ifo research institute showed on Monday.
Sentiment in industry picked up in the second half of 1996, but there are signs of a weakening in the upward trend, the institute said in a report surveying 684 east German companies.
Although businesses expect a significant rise in production -- around 10 percent in 1997 -- they said the decline in jobs, while slowing, was not yet over.
Administrative jobs were the most likely to be cut, Ifo said, pushing more women into unemployment.
By 1996, the average number of jobs in industry in the so-called 'new Laender' of east Germany had plunged to 587,000 from almost 2.8 million in 1990.
Despite extraordinarily high investment in the region, growth in east Germany had not yet reached a level where is was self-sustaining, the report said.

But optimism for the future is increasing, with east German firms expecting 10 percent growth in production this year. The strongest performance was seen in capital goods and in food and consumer goods sectors, where 11 percent growth was expected.
Companies also expected export business to pick up.
Ifo said the 684 firms surveyed employ a total of 92,000 people, around one sixth of those employed in east German industry as a whole.
